question: According to Census 2011, what was the population density of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**382 persons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census 2011, the population density of India was **382 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• The population density is calculated as the number of people per unit area.
 
• It provides a measure of how crowded a place is.
 
• It helps in understanding the distribution of population across different regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census:**

 
 
• The Census is a process of systematically acquiring and recording information about the members of a given population.
 
• In India, the Census is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• The first complete census of India was conducted in 1881.
 
• The Census collects data on various parameters including population size, distribution, and various demographic, social, and economic characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Population Density:**
 
 
• Population density is a measurement of population per unit area or unit volume.
 
• It is commonly represented as people per square kilometer or square mile.
 
• High population density can indicate high urbanization, whereas low population density might indicate rural or less developed areas.
 
• Population density helps in planning and resource allocation by governments and organizations.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Population Density:**
 
 
• Understanding population density is crucial for urban planning and infrastructure development.
